beats.beat: The company is engaged in processing and selling specialty chemicals: Functional Additives (FA), Chemically Modified Minerals (CMM), Soft Minerals (SM), and Hard Minerals (HM). It does not disclose revenue split by product category.
The business model relies on a long-term arrangement with corporate promoter 20 Microns Limited to market and sell products through their established network. This creates dependence on the promoter.

Competitive strengths claimed include a diversified product portfolio, diversified user industries, import substitution, support of the holding company, product innovation and R&D, and a strong management team.
Customer concentration is high: the top 10 customers accounted for around 59%, 57%, and 59% of revenue from operations in FY2015, FY2016, and FY2017 respectively.
The company exports to Nigeria, Saudi Arabia, and Sri Lanka, with past five-year exports of ₹1,068.18 lakh (₹10.68 crore).

beats.beat: The company turned profitable after FY2014: it reported a net loss of ₹27.40 lakh in FY2013 and ₹12.17 lakh in FY2014, then net profits of ₹149.58 lakh in FY2015, ₹90.18 lakh in FY2016, and ₹174.82 lakh in FY2017. For the six months ended September 2017, PAT was ₹132.75 lakh.

Basic EPS mirrored the profit trend: negative in FY2013 and FY2014 (−₹0.45 and −₹0.20), turning positive from FY2015 (₹2.47, ₹1.46, ₹2.43 for FY2015–2017 respectively). For the six months ended Sep 2017, EPS was ₹1.48.

Operating cash flows have been volatile: ₹200.97 lakh in FY2013, ₹127.73 lakh in FY2014, ₹422.36 lakh in FY2015, ₹802.59 lakh in FY2016, but turned sharply negative at ₹−349.75 lakh in FY2017. The six months ended Sep 2017 saw positive cash flow of ₹124.86 lakh.
Total assets as at September 30, 2017 stood at ₹3,424.96 lakh, compared to ₹3,273.96 lakh at March 31, 2017 and ₹3,018.66 lakh at March 31, 2013.
Note: Revenue from operations and debt/equity details are not available in the extracted facts. The report cannot present revenue trend or leverage ratios.

beats.beat: The promoters are individuals Chandresh S. Parikh, Atil C. Parikh, Rajesh C. Parikh, and corporate entity 20 Microns Limited.

Pre-issue shareholding is extremely concentrated: promoters hold 89,48,270 equity shares (99.76% of paid-up capital). The promoter group (excluding promoters) holds the remaining 21,510 shares (0.24%).
The company has a history of related-party transactions with the promoter group for the last five financial years and the six months ended September 30, 2017, as per Accounting Standard 18.

There have been instances of non-filing or delays in filing statutory forms with the Registrar of Companies, and some statutory licenses for a manufacturing facility (Plot 9–10, GIDC Waghodia) have not yet been obtained.
The company, its promoters, group companies, and directors are parties to certain legal proceedings, which could have a material adverse effect if decided unfavourably.

beats.beat: The specialty chemicals segment (excluding agrochemicals and dyestuff) was estimated at around ₹1,000 billion in fiscal 2017, with the broader Indian chemicals industry at ₹5,800–6,200 billion.

The segment grew at 10–12% CAGR from fiscal 2014 to 2017 and is forecast by CRISIL to grow at 12–14% CAGR going forward. Sub-segments like construction chemicals and water chemicals are expected to grow at 15% CAGR.

Demand drivers include increased intensity of consumption, end-use demand from a growing middle class (projected 148 million households by 2030), improved consumption standards, and government initiatives such as the Draft National Chemical Policy and 100% FDI in the sector.
The industry is highly fragmented with SMEs holding 70–75% market share, though few Indian players have the scale to compete with global giants on product development.
Regulatory headwinds include stricter environmental regulations in China (which have reduced output), REACH compliance for EU exports, and the implementation of GST from July 2017.

beats.beat: 20 Microns Nano Minerals Limited processes and sells specialty chemicals including functional additives, chemically modified minerals, and soft/hard minerals. It has a long-term arrangement with its corporate promoter, 20 Microns Limited, to market and sell products through their network.

The company is raising capital through an IPO on the SME Platform of NSE (NSE EMERGE). The lead manager is Vivro Financial Services Private Limited and the registrar is Link Intime India Private Limited.
The primary objects of the issue are to fund capital expenditure for a new manufacturing facility at GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, Gujarat, and for general corporate purposes.

intro.purpose: Orient the reader: who the company is, what it does, what it is raising and why it matters.

beats.beat: The IPO is being lead managed by Vivro Financial Services Private Limited and the registrar is Link Intime India Private Limited.
The issue is being made on the SME Platform of NSE (NSE EMERGE), which is designed for smaller companies with lower listing requirements.

The objects of the issue are: (i) fund capital expenditure for a new manufacturing facility at Plot 336, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, Gujarat; (ii) general corporate purposes; and (iii) creating a public trading market for the equity shares to enhance visibility and brand.
Note: The DRHP does not disclose the fresh issue vs OFS breakdown, selling shareholder names, price band, or issue size in the extracted facts. These are gaps.

beats.beat: Dependence on purchase orders: The company has no long-term or definitive agreements with customers or raw material suppliers. All sales are governed by purchase orders, exposing it to sudden volume or price changes.
Negative operating cash flow in FY2017: Despite profitability, cash flow from operations was strongly negative at ₹−349.75 lakh, which could strain liquidity if sustained.

Missing statutory licenses: The company has not obtained certain required licenses for its manufacturing facility at Plot 9–10, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, and could face penalties or operational disruptions.

High promoter concentration and related-party transactions: Promoters hold 99.76% pre-issue, and related-party transactions have been significant. This creates governance risks and potential conflicts of interest.
Contingent liabilities: As of September 30, 2017, the company had contingent liabilities and commitments aggregating ₹29.11 lakh. If these materialise, they could adversely affect profitability.
